persons.name: Hugh Gallagher
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. THE NAME IS INVENTED TOO, and `name_basis` beside it says so and says which pool it came from: this record used to carry a bare designation instead, on the reasoning that a surname would make it look like the documented layer, but a town of designations does not read as a town and the grade, this note and name_basis all say plainly which layer this is. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE FIRST OF 20 CARPENTER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER RECONSTRUCTS. THE TRADE THE TOWN NEEDED MOST AND THE ONE THE DOCUMENTED LAYER UNDER-COUNTS WORST. The 1835 town census counts 3,265 people in 398 dwellings; Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 describes a settlement of a few dozen buildings, and the reconstruction specification puts 665 roofs on the ground by July 1835. Several hundred of those roofs went up inside eighteen months. Even at a crew of three raising a one-room frame cottage in three weeks, that is on the order of forty carpenter-years of work in a year and a half. Andreas names four carpenters and one ship carpenter in the whole of the 1833 town. Ten carpenter households are inferred against the schedule's eight W2 carpenter-or-joiner shops, because a house carpenter worked on the frame in the street and not in a shop: the shop count is a floor under the trade, not a measure of it. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-14, AND THE ROOF IS THE REASON RATHER THAN A NEW FINDING ABOUT THE TRADE. The count above is stated as a floor in its own last clause, and what held it at ten was method rule 5: every household must be housed, and housing one where no anonymous roof of the right family and district stands means raising an invented building. The block parcel at Randolph and Wells has since put a D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses nine of its ten carpenters in. Adopting it raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record; it puts an argued occupant under a roof that was standing anonymously. Eleven carpenter households are inferred, still against eight W2 shops and still a floor. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-14, ON THE SAME TERMS AND UNDER A RULE THAT NOW HAS THREE TESTS RATHER THAN TWO. The count is still a floor by its own text and still stated against eight W2 shops. The block parcel at Randolph and Market has put a second D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses ten of its eleven carpenters in, and in the division it houses five of them in. The third test is the one T-A4 applied by hand when it refused this trade a roof west of the river; here it passes rather than being waived, which is the difference. Twelve carpenter households are inferred. Adopting the roof raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-15, ON THE SAME TERMS AND UNDER THE SAME THREE TESTS. The count is still a floor by its own text and still stated against eight W2 shops. The block parcel at South Water and Franklin has put a third D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses eleven of its twelve carpenters in, and in the division it houses six of them in. Thirteen carpenter households are inferred. Adopting the roof raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record. WHAT IS NEW HERE IS THE FRONTAGE, AND IT DOES NOT CHANGE THE ANSWER: this is the first block roof adopted on South Water Street, the town's business front, rather than one street back from it. Rule 6 asks about the trade's family and the trade's division and says nothing about which street a roof stands on, deliberately - the roof is a dwelling either way, and a carpenter living on the busiest street in town is not a claim this layer has to argue, because the 665-roof programme already put a dwelling there and the adoption changes only who is under it. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-15, ON THE SAME TERMS AND UNDER THE SAME THREE TESTS. The count is still a floor by its own text and still stated against eight W2 shops. The block parcel at South Water and Wells has put a fourth D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses twelve of its thirteen carpenters in, and in the division it houses seven of them in. Fourteen carpenter households are inferred. Adopting the roof raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record. THE SAME BLOCK OFFERED A SECOND ROOF THIS TRADE PASSES ALL THREE TESTS ON, AND IT WAS REFUSED: the block was also dealt a D4 two-room cottage, and D4 is a family this layer already houses a carpenter in (one, in the North Division), so read literally rule 6 admits it. It is refused because rule 6 opens by saying the mix is a claim about the TOWN rather than about what has been drawn, and taking two roofs for one trade because one block happened to be dealt two of its families is exactly the fitting-the-model-to-the-drawing the rule exists to stop. One roof per trade per block is what every parcel since T-A2h has actually done; this is the first block on which the difference was visible, and ROADMAP K28 is raised to settle whether it is a rule or a habit. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-15, ON THE SAME TERMS AND UNDER THE SAME THREE TESTS. The count is still a floor by its own text and still stated against eight W2 shops. The block parcel at South Water and LaSalle has put a fifth D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses thirteen of its fourteen carpenters in, and in the division it houses eight of them in. Fifteen carpenter households are inferred. Adopting the roof raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record. THE SECOND BLOCK RUNNING HAS OFFERED THIS TRADE A ROOF IT COULD ALSO HAVE TAKEN, AND THE REFUSAL IS T-A9'S: this block was dealt a D4 two-room cottage as well, which is a family this layer houses a carpenter in, so read literally rule 6 admits it. What T-A9 could not know, because it was the first block to meet the case, is that the case is not a one-off - two consecutive blocks have now dealt this trade both of the families it is housed in, which is what turns rule 6's silence from an edge case into a defect. This parcel keeps the conservative reading rather than inventing a second one; ROADMAP K28 is where it is settled, and this block is its second piece of evidence. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-15, ON THE SAME TERMS AND UNDER THE SAME THREE TESTS. The count is still a floor by its own text and still stated against eight W2 shops. The block parcel at South Water and Clark has put a sixth D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses fourteen of its fifteen carpenters in, and in the division it houses nine of them in. Sixteen carpenter households are inferred. Adopting the roof raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record. A THIRD CONSECUTIVE BLOCK HAS DEALT THIS TRADE BOTH OF ITS FAMILIES, AND THE THIRD REFUSAL IS THE ONE THAT SHOULD SETTLE K28: the D4 two-room cottage on lot 2 passes all three tests as literally as the two before it did. T-A9 met the case as an edge, T-A10 found it twice and called it the shape of a South Division block; three for three is no longer evidence that the case recurs but evidence that it is the norm, and a rule that stays silent about the norm is being supplied by habit on every block that lands. Held to one per trade again, on the same conservative reading and as a choice rather than a rule. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-15, ON THE SAME TERMS AND UNDER THE SAME THREE TESTS. The count is still a floor by its own text and still stated against eight W2 shops. The block parcel at South Water and Dearborn has put a seventh D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses fifteen of its sixteen carpenters in, and in the division it houses ten of them in. Seventeen carpenter households are inferred. Adopting the roof raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record. A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE BLOCK HAS DEALT THIS TRADE BOTH OF ITS FAMILIES, AND T-A11 ASKED THAT A FOURTH PRECEDENT NOT BE COLLECTED: the D4 two-room cottage on lot 2 passes all three tests as literally as the three before it did, and T-A11 recorded that three for three had already made the case the ordinary shape of a South Division block rather than a recurring edge. What this parcel adds is therefore not evidence but a measure of how long the question has stood open, and it is the last block of the South Water row to add it: four of the row's five blocks offered this trade a second roof and all four refusals were made on the same conservative reading. Held to one per trade again, as a choice rather than a rule, because settling rule 6 is ROADMAP K28's parcel and not a block parcel's to take. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-15, ON THE SAME TERMS AND UNDER THE SAME THREE TESTS, AND THE FIRST OF THEM OFF SOUTH WATER STREET. The count is still a floor by its own text and still stated against eight W2 shops. The block parcel at Lake and Market has put an eighth D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses sixteen of its seventeen carpenters in, and in the division it houses eleven of them in. Eighteen carpenter households are inferred. Adopting the roof raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record. THE SECOND-ROOF QUESTION SURVIVES THE END OF THE SOUTH WATER ROW, WHICH IS WHAT THIS BLOCK ADDS TO IT: the D4 two-room cottage on lot 4 passes all three tests as literally as the four before it did, and T-A11 read three consecutive cases as evidence that the double candidacy is the ordinary shape of a South WATER block. It is not. This is the first block of the parcel shape on a different street, one row back, and it deals the same pair - so the case rule 6 is silent about is the ordinary shape of a South Division block of five dwellings, wherever it stands, and the sample K28 has to settle is larger than the row that produced it. Held to one per trade again, as a choice rather than a rule, because settling rule 6 is ROADMAP K28's parcel and not a block parcel's to take. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-15, ON THE SAME TERMS AND UNDER THE SAME THREE TESTS. The count is still a floor by its own text and still stated against eight W2 shops. The block parcel at Randolph and Franklin has put a ninth D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses seventeen of its eighteen carpenters in, and in the division it houses twelve of them in. Nineteen carpenter households are inferred. Adopting the roof raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record. THE SECOND-ROOF QUESTION IS NOT WHAT SIX BLOCKS HAVE CALLED IT, AND THIS IS THE FINDING THIS BLOCK ADDS RATHER THAN A SEVENTH PRECEDENT. Every block of this shape since T-A9 has recorded the D4 it was dealt as a SECOND roof for the carpenters and refused it on a conservative reading. The D4 two-room cottage on lot 0 here passes all three tests as literally as the five before it did and is refused on the same reading. But the D4 is also the FIRST roof of the teamsters, who are one of the four trades method rule 2 argues from the town's building rate rather than from a roof cap, who are housed in D4 and in no other family, and who this layer already places in the South Division - so it passes all three tests for them too, and no parcel has ever said so. Sixteen anonymous D2 and D4 roofs now stand in the South Division under exactly this description. What K28 has to settle is therefore larger than six blocks of one question: it is whether rule 6 admits a roof for a trade that has not asked for it. Held to one per trade again, as a choice rather than a rule, because settling rule 6 is ROADMAP K28's parcel and not a block parcel's to take. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-15, ON THE SAME TERMS AND UNDER THE SAME THREE TESTS, AND IT IS THE BACKFILL RATHER THAN A NEW BLOCK. The count is still a floor by its own text and still stated against eight W2 shops. blk_randolph_dearborn landed on 2026-08-14, before rule 6 had its third test and before the household question was asked of a block at all, so its five dwellings have stood unexamined ever since; ROADMAP T-A3h is the parcel that examines them. Its D3 one-room frame cottage on lot 0 is a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses eighteen of its nineteen carpenters in, and in the division it houses thirteen of them in. Twenty carpenter households are inferred. Adopting the roof raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record. THE SECOND ROOF IS REFUSED FOR THE SEVENTH TIME AND FOR THE FIRST TIME WITH ITS EVIDENCE TRACED, AND THAT TRACE IS THIS PARCEL'S FINDING RATHER THAN THE ADOPTION. The D4 two-room cottage on lot 6 passes all three tests as literally as the six before it did - tools/measure_adoption_tests.py D4 south prints ADOPTABLE for the carpenters and for no one else. What no parcel had asked is WHERE the D4 half of that verdict comes from. This layer houses exactly one carpenter in a D4: hh_inf_carpenter_north_10, in inf_carpenter_dwelling_north, which stands in the NORTH Division. All thirteen carpenters it houses in the SOUTH Division are in a D3. So the candidacy is assembled from a family taken out of one division and a division taken out of another family, and this layer has never housed a carpenter in a D4 in the South Division - nor can it, until some parcel adopts one and makes it true. Rule 6 states in its own text that the three tests are independent, so the literal reading admits the roof and the refusal stands as the same choice the six before it made. What changes is K28's question: before deciding how many roofs of a block a trade may take, it has to decide whether rule 6's table is a set of (family, division) PAIRS or two projections of one. Measured with tools/measure_adoption_tests.py --pairs; nothing is decided here.

METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure.
